summaries.title: Is Long-Term Stock Market Momentum Slowing In A Concerning Manner?
summaries.reason: The video concludes the secular bull market remains intact: monthly and quarterly RSI are in strong (70+) territory, breadth is broadening constructively, credit (BKLN) is confirming new highs, and the model trend score is back to double 100.
summaries.summary: Chris Ciovacco asks whether long-term stock market momentum is slowing in a concerning manner and concludes it is not. On the monthly Nasdaq chart, momentum (RSI) closed at a strong 70.11 on August 7 despite the recent tech/AI stall — far above readings that characterized the 2000-2013 secular stagnation period. Quarterly RSI for the S&P 500 sits above 70, resembling prior secular bull markets (1982-2000) rather than stagnation windows, with price well above an upward-sloping 10-quarter moving average. The S&P 500 trades above rising 50-, 150-, and 200-day moving averages, and the NYSE composite shows a full-board bullish moving-average stack. Breadth is constructive: the S&P 500 advance/decline volume line is above its Bollinger centerline, mid-cap growth is making new highs above a rising 200-week MA, and the travel/tourism index jumped 9.5% in five sessions. Credit confirms the move — leveraged loans (BKLN) printed a new high. Even laggards like small caps and the S&P 1500 look healthy in absolute terms, though they remain in relative downtrends, so large-cap leadership persists. Gold remains a long-term holding but faces short-term overhead resistance; patience is advised before adding. The models (136 charts, 489 binary questions) read constructive, and the trend score is back to double 100. Bottom line: the secular bull market is intact; stay patient and keep an open, unbiased mind.
